intro_en: In this lesson you learn to say where things and people are: "There is a bed in the room", "There is a dog in the garden", "Mother is in the kitchen". The key difference is あります for non-living things and います for living things. You will also learn position words such as on top, under, in front, behind, inside and next to, and や〜など for listing examples ("a desk, a chair and so on"). The vocabulary for this lesson covers the house, rooms, furniture and pets.

g10-1.explanation_en: Japanese has two verbs for "there is / is (somewhere)": あります (ある) for non-living things, plants and events; います (いる) for living things that move by themselves, such as people, animals and birds. Tamil shows the difference with a respect ending, as in "புத்தகம் இருக்கிறது" (the book is there) / "அம்மா இருக்கிறார்" (Mother is there), but in Japanese the verb itself changes. が marks who or what is there; it is the が that introduces new information (like 時間があります in Lesson 9). Negative: ありません / いません. Careful: flowers and trees are alive, but they don't move, so they take あります.
g10-1.tamil_parallel_en: Tamil uses one verb இருக்கிறது ("is there") for both, while Japanese splits it by living vs non-living: நாய் இருக்கிறது ("there is a dog") = 犬がいます; மேசை இருக்கிறது ("there is a desk") = 机があります.
g10-1.formation_en: N(non-living) + が + あります / ありません ／ N(living) + が + います / いません
g10-1.pitfalls_en: 犬があります ✗. Animals take います. 花がいます ✗. Flowers don't move, so あります. Because Tamil uses "இருக்கிறது" (is there) for both, this mistake happens often.

g10-2.explanation_en: To show where something is, add に after the place: 部屋にベッドがあります = "There is a bed in the room". This is the job of the Tamil "-இல்" (the seventh case ending). This pattern introduces something new to the listener: "What is in the room? There is a bed." The order is the same as Tamil: place → thing → is there. Careful: in Lesson 6 you saw で for the place where an action happens (喫茶店で飲みます), but for existence (あります/います) it is always に. In Tamil both are "-இல்", so be careful. Questions: 何がありますか (What is there?), 誰がいますか (Who is there?).
g10-2.tamil_parallel_en: に for where something exists matches the Tamil locative -இல், in the same order: அறையில்(-இல்) கட்டில் இருக்கிறது ("there is a bed in the room") = 部屋にベッドがあります.
g10-2.formation_en: N(place) + に + N + が + あります / います
g10-2.pitfalls_en: 部屋でベッドがあります ✗. Existence takes に. 何はありますか ✗. After a question word, use が (何が / 誰が).

g10-3.explanation_en: To say where something already known (already being talked about) is, make it the topic with は and give the place with に: 母は台所にいます = "(As for) Mother, she is in the kitchen". In g10-2, the pattern was "place → what is there", introducing new information; here it is "thing → where it is", so the place is the new information. It is like the Tamil difference between "சமையலறையில் ஒரு ஃப்ரிட்ஜ் இருக்கிறது" (there is a fridge in the kitchen) and "ஃப்ரிட்ஜ் சமையலறையில் இருக்கிறது" (the fridge is in the kitchen). Question: トイレはどこにありますか (Where is the toilet?). The simple form トイレはあそこです from Lesson 3 gives the same meaning.
g10-3.tamil_parallel_en: Putting the known thing first, as in Tamil, makes the place the new information: அம்மா சமையலறையில் இருக்கிறார் ("Mother is in the kitchen") = 母は台所にいます; கழிவறை எங்கே இருக்கிறது? ("Where is the toilet?") = トイレはどこにありますか.
g10-3.formation_en: N + は + N(place) + に + あります / います  (= N は 場所 です)
g10-3.pitfalls_en: You can also say 母が台所にいます, but only as an answer to "Who is there?". If someone asks "Where is Mother?", answer with は: 母は〜.

g10-4.explanation_en: To say "on the desk" or "under the bed": base noun + の + position word + に. 机の上に = "on (top of) the desk". This matches the Tamil "மேசையின் மேல்" (on the desk), built with "-இன்" (the sixth case ending, "of") + "மேல்" (top), perfectly: の = "-இன்", 上 = "மேல்", に = "-இல்". Words: 上 (on / above), 下 (under / below), 前 (in front), 後ろ (behind), 中 (inside), 右 (right), 左 (left), 隣 (next to, for things of the same kind side by side), 近く (near), 間 (between: AとBの間 = "between A and B"). These are nouns, so の before them is required.
g10-4.tamil_parallel_en: The Japanese order matches the Tamil genitive -இன் + position word: மேசையின் மேல் ("on the desk") = 机の上に; வங்கியின் பக்கத்தில் ("next to the bank") = 銀行の隣に; வங்கிக்கும் தபால் நிலையத்துக்கும் இடையில் ("between the bank and the post office") = 銀行と郵便局の間に.
g10-4.formation_en: N1 + の + 上 / 下 / 前 / 後ろ / 中 / 右 / 左 / 隣 / 近く + に ／ N1 と N2 の 間 に
g10-4.pitfalls_en: 机上に ✗ / 机に上 ✗. The order is 机 + の + 上 + に. Remember the Tamil order "மேசை-இன் மேல்-இல்" (desk-of top-at). 隣 is for things of the same kind (shop next to shop, house next to house); for the general meaning "near", use 近く.

g10-5.explanation_en: と from Lesson 4 ("A and B") gives a complete list; that's all there is. や means "A, B and so on": there are more, and these are only examples. Adding など (etc. / and so on) after the last item makes this feeling even clearer: 机や椅子などがあります = "There are a desk, chairs and so on". It is like the Tamil "மேசை, நாற்காலி முதலியன" (desk, chair, etc.). や joins only nouns, not sentences.
g10-5.tamil_parallel_en: や〜など works like the Tamil போன்றவை / முதலியன ("and so on") after a list of examples: மேசை, நாற்காலி போன்றவை இருக்கின்றன ("there are desks, chairs and so on") = 机や椅子などがあります.
g10-5.pitfalls_en: If the room has only a desk and a chair, use と; if there are other things too, use や. Don't use や with verbs or adjectives.

g10-6.explanation_en: In Lesson 4 you saw ね used to ask for the agreement of the listener, like "isn't it?". Here is another job it does in conversation: repeating information you just heard to confirm it. If someone says 冷蔵庫は台所にあります, the listener checks with 台所ですね ("The kitchen, right?"). It is like saying "சமையலறையில் தானே?" (in the kitchen, right?) or "இரண்டாம் மாடி இல்லையா?" (the second floor, isn't it?) in Tamil. It is very useful when asking for directions or looking for something in a shop. Notice the difference between ですか (a question: you don't know) and ですね (confirming: you more or less know). よ from Lesson 5 (giving new information) is the opposite of this.
g10-6.tamil_parallel_en: Confirming ね matches the Tamil tag தானே / இல்லையா ("right? / isn't it?"): சமையலறையில் தானே? ("in the kitchen, right?") = 台所ですね; இரண்டாம் மாடி இல்லையா? ("the second floor, isn't it?") = 二階ですね.
g10-6.formation_en: A: 〜は どこに ありますか。 B: 〜に あります。 A: 〜ですね。
g10-6.pitfalls_en: If you say よ instead of ね when confirming (二階ですよ), it sounds like you are giving the other person information: "It's the second floor, you know!"

items.L10-q01: 冷蔵庫 = れいぞうこ (ஃப்ரிட்ஜ், refrigerator). Both れい and ぞう are long sounds; 蔵 = ぞう (voiced). Dropping either one is wrong.
items.L10-q02: 台所 = だいどころ (சமையலறை, kitchen). 所 alone is ところ, but here it becomes voiced as どころ. Reading たい without the voiced mark is wrong.
items.L10-q03: 玄関 = げんかん (வாசல், entrance). げ is voiced, かん is not voiced.
items.L10-q04: いぬ = 犬 (நாய், dog): 大 + a dot at the top right. 太 (ふとい) = 大 + a dot below; 天 (てん) has a line on top. These kanji look similar.
items.L10-q05: みぎ = 右 (வலது, right). 左 (ひだり = இடது, left) has 工 at the bottom; 右 has 口 at the bottom. 石 (いし) and 有 (ある) look similar.
items.L10-q06: The place with lots of books = 本棚 (புத்தக அலமாரி, bookshelf). 冷蔵庫 is for food; 玄関 and 門 are entrances.
items.L10-q07: The place where you keep milk = 冷蔵庫 (ஃப்ரிட்ஜ், refrigerator), with 〜の中に (inside). Milk wouldn't be "inside" the others.
items.L10-q08: Dogs, cats and similar animals = pets (ペット, செல்லப்பிராணி). 鳥 is only one example; 家族 and 子供 are people.
items.L10-q09: Two houses side by side = 隣 (பக்கத்து வீடு, next door). Another house can't be 中, 上 or 下 of a house.
items.L10-q10: The place where the cat sleeps = on the ベッド (கட்டில், bed): の上. 冷蔵庫, 門 and トイレ are not places to sleep. Here the action is 寝ます, so it takes で; for existence (います) it would be に.
items.L10-q11: It says "not on the desk", so it is under = 下 (கீழ், under). 中 (inside) doesn't fit a desk.
items.L10-q12: The desk is in front of the chair = the chair is behind the desk (机の後ろに椅子, மேசையின் பின்னால் நாற்காலி). 机の前に椅子 is a common mistake that swaps the positions.
items.L10-q13: N は 場所に います = 場所に N が います: the same information, only the emphasis differs. 寝ます is a different action; いません is negative.
items.L10-q14: Nobody is there = there are no people (人はいません, ஆட்கள் இல்லை). 誰かいます (யாரோ இருக்கிறார், someone is there) is the opposite; 静か is only a guess, not the same meaning.
items.L10-q15: A dog is a living thing → います (இருக்கிறது, is there). あります is only for non-living things; the trap is that Tamil uses "இருக்கிறது" for both.
items.L10-q16: A flower is alive but doesn't move → あります (இருக்கிறது, is there). います is for animals and people. ありますか is a question, but this is a statement.
items.L10-q17: The place of existence (あります) → に. で is for the place where an action happens (部屋で寝ます), not for existence.
items.L10-q18: 机の上 = "மேசையின் மேல்" (on the desk); の = the Tamil "-இன்". 机に上 is a word-order mistake.
items.L10-q19: A question about あります (things) → 何 (என்ன, what). 誰 goes with います, for people; どこ asks about a place, but the place has already been given.
items.L10-q20: An incomplete list with など (போன்றவை, and so on) → や. と is for a complete list; や is the natural partner of など.
items.L10-q21: Repeating information you heard to confirm it → ですね ("இரண்டாம் மாடி தானே", the second floor, right?). ですよ gives information; it is not natural for the person receiving the information to say it.
items.L10-q22: かばんは (topic) → 椅子の下に (நாற்காலியின் கீழ், under the chair) → あります. ★ = 下に.
items.L10-q23: Place (駅の近くに) → list (銀行や喫茶店などが) → あります. ★ = 銀行や; や comes after the first item and など after the last item.
items.L10-q24: ドアの後ろに (கதவின் பின்னால், behind the door) → 誰か (யாரோ, someone) → います → よ. ★ = 誰か. 誰か is a living person, so it takes います.
items.L10-q25: ［1］With や, the list ends with など (போன்றவை, and so on). ［2］猫 is a living thing → います. ［3］The place of existence (います) → に; で is only for the place where an action happens.
